title: Reduced left-resolution datum from a class of covers
statement: Let $A$ be an abelian category [def-sp-abelian]. Let $\mathcal F$ be a class of objects containing zero and closed under isomorphisms, finite biproducts and direct summands. Suppose $P:A\to A$ has values in $\mathcal F$ and $\epsilon:P\Rightarrow\operatorname{id}_A$ has epimorphic components. Then there exist a preadditive category $C$ with a zero object and finite coproducts, a fully faithful additive functor $\iota:C\to A$ with $\iota(X)\in\mathcal F$ for every object $X$ of $C$, a functor $Q:A\to C$ preserving zero morphisms, and a natural transformation $\pi: \iota Q\Rightarrow\operatorname{id}_A$ with epimorphic components.

proof.text: Let C be the full subcategory of A whose objects are exactly the members of F, and let iota:C \to A be its inclusion. Since A is abelian [def-sp-abelian], it is preadditive and has a zero object and finite biproducts; because F contains zero and is closed under finite biproducts, C inherits a zero object and finite coproducts (which are biproducts in a preadditive category), and iota is fully faithful and additive. The inclusion has iota(X) in F by construction. The ambient category A is idempotent complete by [lem-sfb-abelian-idempotent-complete]. If an idempotent in C splits in A, its retract object is a direct summand of an object of F, hence lies in F; fullness then makes the splitting maps morphisms of C. Thus C is idempotent complete as well.

proof.text: Regard P as a functor Q0:A \to C by taking Q0(M) to be the same object P(M), now equipped with its membership in F, and taking its action on morphisms from P. The given epsilon is then a natural transformation iota Q0 \Rightarrow id_A with epimorphic components, so (Q0, epsilon) is a LeftResolution of iota. Apply the reduced left-resolution API [lem-sfb-left-resolution-reduced-api] to this datum and the idempotent-complete categories A and C. Its reduced resolution supplies a functor Q:A -> C preserving zero morphisms and a natural transformation pi:iota Q \Rightarrow id_A with epimorphic components. Since every object of C was chosen from F, iota(X) lies in F for all X, giving all the required data.
